title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
This is a collision between an autonomous vehicle and an animal in its path, on a public residential street. The vehicle was operated by Avride in Austin, Texas, and the company confirmed it was in autonomous mode at the time. A human safety operator was present in the vehicle. The failure sits where a driving system decides what in the road counts as an obstacle requiring a response, and where a safety operator is meant to catch what the system does not.

Catching it would have required the system to register a small animal in the vehicle's path as something to brake for, and would have required the operator to intervene in time. The reporting does not establish that either happened. Avride's response was to exclude certain streets around the lake from its testing area and to work on technology improvements aimed at preventing similar situations, while continuing to test on other public roads.

What is not established: the account that the car ran over the duck without slowing or stopping comes from a resident's social media post, not from a company finding. Avride said it found no evidence supporting a separate resident claim that the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign. Whether the vehicle's system detected the duck at all is not established.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride in Austin, Texas struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood, prompting significant community backlash. A resident reported on social media that the self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, ran over the duck without slowing down or stopping. The incident garnered local media attention partly because residents were familiar with this particular duck, which had been nesting near a local restaurant. Concerned neighbors have since placed the duck's eggs in an incubator to preserve them.

Following the incident, Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode and stated it found no evidence supporting a resident's claim that the car failed to stop at a stop sign. The company has adjusted its testing area by excluding certain streets around the lake and is now working on technology improvements to prevent similar situations. Avride continues testing autonomous vehicles on other public roads, while other companies like Waymo, Tesla, and Zoox also operate self-driving vehicles in Austin.
title_en: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck
